Subject: US/EU/APAC service interruption — temporary reroute instructions & follow-up

Hi Amit / Nimbus ops team,

Quick note to acknowledge what you may have seen in the last 20 minutes: we've detected elevated error rates and increased tail latency for inference requests routed through two of our cloud provider regions that host pieces of Redwood Dedicated (impacting US-West1, EU-Central and an APAC POP). Our SREs are actively investigating the provider-side networking disruption.

Immediate impact: some customer requests failed with 502/504 or experienced >2x latency. We are not seeing model corruption or data leakage. All request logs are being retained.

Temporary mitigation we recommend for your stack (actionable, shortest path):
- If possible, update your endpoint target to our regional fallback endpoints which route to unaffected capacity:
  • us-fallback.redwoodapi.com (preferred for US traffic)
  • eu-fallback.redwoodapi.com (preferred for EU traffic)
  • apac-fallback.redwoodapi.com (preferred for APAC traffic)
- Set a retry policy with exponential backoff and 3 retries for idempotent requests.
- If you use pinned model versions, falling back to the compatible quantized model (v1.3-q4) will reduce latency while preserving correctness.

We have attached a short manifest with the logs we've collected so far (incident-snapshot-20260908-manifest.txt). Our team will provide a post-incident packet including packet captures and timing tables within 48 hours upon request.

Next steps from Redwood:
- SRE will publish an interim status update at +30m and a containment confirmation when traffic normalizes.
- Postmortem and root cause within 72 hours.

If you want immediate hand-holding, reply with a preferred time and we can open a short bridge with our SRE (I can include Laura and Karthik).

Sorry for the interruption — we know this hits critical paths and we're prioritizing customers with active traffic.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Incident update: containment confirmed and next steps (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Amit — quick follow-up with a containment summary and next steps.

What happened (brief):
- Root cause: transient cross-region peering congestion at our cloud vendor that affected a subset of POPs used by Redwood Dedicated’s sidecar routing mesh. The vendor confirmed a misconfigured BGP flap which caused intermittent packet loss between POPs.
- Impact window: ~08:05–09:40 PDT for the majority of affected flows; limited residual tail latency until ~12:50 PDT.

Customer-facing actions taken:
- We proactively routed traffic away from the affected POPs and activated warm standby capacity.
- Published short-term fallback endpoints to reduce request surface area.
- Added automatic retry with jitter at the service edge for idempotent requests.

What we validated:
- No customer payloads were written to vendor-managed persistent blobs during the window (confirmed by storage team at 08:45).
- Model state and KV caches were intact; no regeneration required.

Deliverables we will provide:
- Post-incident packet (48 hours): request-id map, per-request timing histograms, packet captures, and vendor incident number.
- SOC2 evidence subset on request (we can redact sensitive traces).

Attached: nimbus-request-evidence.zip (log summaries and request-id index). Shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Incident-20260908-logs (read access granted to ops@nimbushealth.com).

If you'd like a short 20-minute review call to walk through the packet, I can schedule with Karthik and Laura this afternoon. Please reply with a time slot.

Appreciate your patience — we're treating this with high priority.

Best,
Olga
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
